summary: Help children aged 5-6 become fluent at adding and subtracting within 5 (e.g. 2+3, 5-2, 3-3, 4+0), where fluency means accurate, efficient and flexible recall built from subitising and part-whole understanding — not raw speed. The primary engine is short, frequent, low-stakes retrieval practice with quantity images (five-frames, dice/domino patterns, fingers) kept attached until recall is secure, interleaving addition with its inverse subtraction and including the +0/-0 case.
misconceptions: Counting from 1 on fingers for every fact, never moving to recall — fluency stalls.
Equating fluency with speed and rushing, producing errors, or freezing under time pressure.
Knowing additions but not the related subtractions within 5.
Uncertainty with 0 (thinking 3 + 0 must change the number).
Over-reliance on one strategy (always counting on) rather than recognising known facts.

activities.title: Quick-flash fact practice from a dot pattern
steps: A five-frame, dice or domino pattern (e.g. four dots) appears briefly, then the child says or taps the answer to a fact tied to it (e.g. 4 + 1, or 5 − 1 from the same image).
Keep answering a short daily set of items in a few minutes, mixing addition and subtraction.
When a fact is answered quickly and correctly, show the image more briefly next time; when the child hesitates or errs, re-show the pattern longer and talk through what they see.
Include zero cases such as 4 + 0 and 3 − 3 in the mix.
activities.insight: A child can stop counting dots one by one and simply KNOW a pattern's value, then flip the same image into a subtraction (5 − 1 = 4). Recall becomes meaningful because it is anchored to an instantly-recognisable quantity image.

activities.title: Periodic low-stakes fact check
steps: Work through a short set of image-supported fact items (multiple-choice or fill-the-blank) that interleave addition and subtraction within 5, including a zero case.
Treat this as an occasional check of what has become automatic, not the daily practice engine.
After answering, note which facts were known instantly and which were worked out.
activities.insight: Children and adults can see which within-5 facts are now recalled automatically and which still need practice, especially any subtraction or zero facts that lag.

activities.title: Oral quick-fire warm-up and subitising reference
steps: Run a brief spoken quick-fire: 'What's 2 and 3? … 5 take away 2? … 4 and 1? … 3 take away 3?' and have the child answer aloud fast.
Ask follow-up reasoning prompts: 'Which of those did you just know, and which did you work out?', 'If 2 + 3 = 5, what is 5 − 3?', 'What happens if I add 0 to 4?'
Keep a reference chart of subitisable patterns 0-5 (five-frames, dice/dot patterns) visible to glance at when recall is uncertain.
activities.insight: Talking through which facts were known versus worked out surfaces the move from counting to recall, and connects each subtraction to its related addition.

checkQuestion: Quick answers, try not to count on your fingers: what is 2 + 3? … 5 − 2? … 4 + 1? … 3 − 3?
checkAnswer: 5, 3, 5, 0 — answered quickly from recall or subitising, without laborious counting from one.
